output.title: Peer-to-Peer Review Scheduling Window After a Prior Authorization Denial
output.draft_text:
Q: How many days does a prescriber have to schedule a peer-to-peer review after a denial?

A: After a prior authorization or coverage denial, the prescriber has [number of days] [calendar/business days] to request a peer-to-peer review. The window starts on [start event, e.g., date of the denial decision or date of the denial notice].

How the prescriber requests it: The prescriber or their office contacts [contact method, e.g., phone number, fax, or portal] and gives [required information, e.g., member ID, denial reference number, drug name]. The review is scheduled with [reviewer type, e.g., clinical pharmacist or physician reviewer], usually within [number of days/hours] of the request.

If the window has passed: The prescriber can no longer request a peer-to-peer for this denial. They can [alternative options, e.g., submit a formal appeal or a new prior authorization request]. The deadline for a formal appeal is [appeal deadline].

Exceptions: [Note any differences by plan type, line of business, state rule, or urgent/expedited cases, or remove this section if none apply.]

What the advocate should tell the member: Explain that the prescriber, not the member, must request the peer-to-peer. Encourage the member to contact their prescriber's office promptly so the deadline is not missed.
